text: A refusal of the placement admission answers 403 with MSG-P4-002 and one reason code: RIGHT_NOT_HELD for a missing C letter in Queue and allocation, CALLER_KIND for a subject that does not resolve to a role of class NON_HUMAN_ACTOR, and SCOPE_NOT_ALL for an admitting role whose default scope is not ALL. An empty or out-of-range field keeps its own 422 with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-GEN-002, an unrecorded entry keeps its 503 with MSG-P7-003, and the 403 returns the area, the letter, the matrix version and the scope and nothing else.
why: One message serves four different causes in the sources, and an adapter and an operator must be able to tell them apart without parsing prose; no source names a reason code vocabulary, so the story fixes one and keeps the legacy message texts unchanged.

text: Constraint names follow the platform naming convention, the primary key is on id, role.role_code is unique, permission.role_id is the only foreign key, and one index per read path is created with the leading columns permission (role_id, capability_area), masking_rule (role_code, field_id, masking_version), role_conflict (role_code, conflict_version) and delegation_limit (decision_code, regulation_item, product_group, valid_from).
why: No source names the constraints or the index columns, and the read paths of the service name the predicates but not an index.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 and T3.3; the read paths of RWB-P4-E2013-APP, RWB-P4-E1019-APP and the masking answer; WP B-P4-12
confirm: ACE team (suggested; any team may pick up this story), at the DDL review
impact: An index added or renamed later is a change on the same service sequence; the plan check of AC10 is the guard.

text: role.entra_group is kept as a nullable varchar(120) column with Field ID DF-REF-039, and the Entra group mapping is read at run time through the rwb-source-data contract instead of from this column, so no ACE fact is copied or maintained here.
why: The technical specification gives the column a Field ID and the functional specification calls the group a view field and not a Workbench column; the technical specification outranks the functional one in R-PREC, and neither reading allows a maintained copy of an ACE fact.
read: TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-039); FSD P4 v3 change note and field catalog; R-PREC precedence table
confirm: Solution architect, with the ACE team
impact: If the column is dropped later, one dictionary row and one column go with it, and the run-time read is unchanged because it already comes from the contract.

text: This story declares its 44 dictionary rows as a build artefact (entity, field, Field ID, data type, physical type, data product), the conformance test compares rwb_access with that declaration, and the one dictionary in rwb_source_data carries the rows through its own seed; this service writes no row of rwb_source_data.
why: The dictionary is one dictionary of 122 objects and 1,366 rows in rwb_source_data under the P1 ruling, so a per-service dictionary write would be the cross-schema write DP-01 forbids, yet the split still needs the field rows of each schema to be complete and matched.
read: RWB-P1-E1001-APP sections 1, 11 and 13; legacy RWB-E1-001 sections 11 and 13; DP-01
confirm: Data steward and data product owner (RW-DATASTEW), with the P1 dictionary owner
impact: If the dictionary is later split per service, the declaration becomes the service's own seed and the handover step of section 13 becomes a migration on this story's sequence.
